after.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =3+\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5-0}\cdot (3+\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}+\frac{\pi }{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=3-2x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $1.$
content.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(3-2x)\,\text{d}x \\ 1 & ={\frac{1}{c}(3x-{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{c} \\ 1 & =\frac{1}{c}[(3c-{c}^{2})-(0)] \\ 1 & =3-c \\ -2 & =-c \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$
